ETA hand2mind Connecting People, Set of 96 This educational toy consists of small, easily swallowed pieces, making it a choking hazard. Thus, it is not recommended for children younger than age 5 and should be kept well away from pets, especially puppies who like to chew things. This toy is recommended for grades K-4, which is approximately ages 5-9. It's primary purpose is helping children learn counting. They can also use it to learn to sort and classify.

The set includes 96 pieces of sturdy, plastic, free-standing, girl and boy figures. Half are male and half female. The pieces come in three sizes, each in four colors, yellow, red, green and blue. The sizes are all rather small, ranging from only 1/2 inch to 1 inch in height. The larger figures weigh about 3-4 grams and the smallest figures weigh about 1 gram. The figures are well made in terms of having smooth surfaces, which is important to avoid harming small fingers. The figures are stored in a zip-lock type plastic bag.

As advertised, the pieces do stand up by themselves, and they can be linked together. However, it can be difficult for younger children to clip them together. They each have a protruding peg on one hand and a hole on the other hand. It takes hand-eye coordination to match up a peg and a hole, and some finger strength to shove a peg into a hole. Taking them apart is even harder. Thus, this toy can be frustrating to kids on the younger end of the recommended age range, 5-6 years old, and is most likely to be handled smoothly by children on the higher end of the scale, age 7-9. Some of these problems might have been avoided if the figures came in larger sizes.
text_fidelity_b: ETA hand2mind Connecting People, Set of 96

text_fidelity_a:
Pressman Tri-Ominos - Deluxe Edition Triangular Tiles with Brass Spinners, 5" I’ve always wanted Tri-Ominos because it is a twist on Dominos but uses triangular instead of rectangular tiles and it's lots of fun.

WHAT'S IN THE BOX:
56 triangular tiles
4 plastic tile holders (or racks)
1 instruction sheet

The object of the game is to be the first player to score 400 points with each game consisting of several rounds of play.

For example, with two players, nine tiles are given to each player. The tiles should be face down so that the other player or players don’t see them. Each player adds up the numbers on each of their tiles. If a player has a tile with three of the same numbers on the tile, then the player with the highest combination goes first. For example , a player with three 5’s (which is equal to 15) would go before a player with three 4’s (which is 12) and score the bonus points explained in the instruction card. If no player has a Tri-Omino tile, then the player with the highest numbered tiled goes first but no bonus points would be given.

The idea is for a player to match his or her tile to a tile on the board that has two of the same numbers. They basically get connected the way that it is done with Dominos. The score gets added up for each tile placed. Those that can’t make a match pick from the “well” or remaining face down tiles. Each pick from the well cost the player 5 points from their score. If you can’t match any Tri-Omino in your hand and the well is empty, ten points are deducted from your score and the play continues.

The first player to play all of his Tri-Ominos wins the round and receives a 25-point bonus plus the total points of all the Tri-Ominos left in the other players’ hands. If the game is blocked, then the player with the least amount of tiles wins and gets to add all the points from the left over tiles to their score but there are no bonus points given. This player must also deduct the total number of points that were left in his hand from his score. This method of play gets repeated until a player reaches 400 points to win the game. There are a few other ways to get bonus points in a game as well.

Scoring is done after every play, so from this perspective the game can be tedious. However, it is a lot of fun and for young children, the process of adding up the numbers on the tiles is an education in math. My boyfriend and I really love this game. Playing a full game with two people takes a couple of hours.
text_fidelity_b: Pressman Tri-Ominos - Deluxe Edition Triangular Tiles with Brass Spinners, 5"

AMIGO X-Code Cooperative Strategy Board Game, Black This is very different from anything we have played before. It is very quick to learn and very quick to play. I love that it is cooperative which keeps most hurt feelings down. It played well at a range of ages from 11 to 51 which was also fantastic. All in all, I am very impressed with this game.

The play is very easy...at first. Basically, you are passing cards to help each other make sets and cover the numbers on a phone keypad. There are rules governing how to pass and who to pass too and lots of communication as you try to get cards where they need to go. You can also make sets of cards that allow you to extend your game by flipping your one minute timer. We found the first round pretty easy actually, and then came the twists... It has a good variety of challenges that make a nice straight forward game more challenging.

I highly recommend this game. There are few games that can be learned so quickly, play accross some many ages, and be so fun and engaging. They hit it all on this one.

Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over This game is best for really young children! I'd say 2-4. My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over

It looks good, has a smooth ride, with a snazzy traditional bell to alert the neighbors.That's all good, but it needs more work at the design level.

The handlebars don't seem to attach securely, but not unsafely. A 3 year-old might not be able to loosen them, but any adult certainly can. Tighten them as hard as you can.

The cover for the handlebars -- where it attaches to the headset (just above the wheel) pops off whenever the wheel is turned. It is intended to, and does, snap in when still, but should remain snapped in always.

The bike is designed, per the packaging, for 2.5-5 year-olds. My boy turns 3 in three weeks and is considered average height. He's slightly too small. Instead, the age guidelines should describe height, not age, or both. He'll grow into it so I'm not concerned.

Overall, I'll keep it, but if I were to buy a new one, I'd buy one fully assembled, maybe even used, to ensure everything was solidly connected.

Anthony Trendl
TreeFortBooks.com

Bugs in the Kitchen - Children's Board Game, Standard, 6 - 15 years My boys have had tons of fun with this game. I like it, too.

The set up is super easy, as well as playing the game. You basically put a thick cardboard piece in place, and a couple of tubes, and you're all set. It also comes with a hexbug and 12 various colored (non-moving)bugs. Each player will get 3 of those, and the goal is to get all 3 bugs to the other side first. The hexbug moves around under the board, through the tubes, and on the playing board. While he's on the playing board, you have to stop playing, and hope that he doesn't knock your bug out of place. If he does knock your bug completely off its spot, it has to go back to the beginning(after he's went off the upper board).

The only negative is the fact that the hexbug uses a button cell battery. We don't keep those things around typically, so in order to keep this game going, we'll now have to. It's still a very fun and easy game, though.

It's labeled for 6 and up, but my 3 and 5 year old children have loved it, too, along with my 8 year old. I'm guessing the 6 and up is due to a possible choking hazard, because it's a simple game to play.

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. Okay, so I got the kit and made the TWO potholders. I bought this kit because the loom was metal, and I'd read reviews and seen videos where the person's PLASTIC loom would break. So, what's the problem?
I really don't like how the loops slip off this loom, especially when you're getting towards completing the project. Pop, pop, pop go the loops - OFF the loom! This might be the nature of pot-holder looming, but I think the problem is the little spokes (hooks) are straight, so there's nothing to keep the loops from slipping off. They should be curved and WIDER at the top so the loops can't slide off. Towards the end, when you're crocheting the edges together, the last side can get completely unraveled.
THAT IS frustrating.
I'm going to try to find another loom.
Unfortunately, I looked at a lot looms before I bought this one, and they ALL seem to have the same design flaw.

Afterthought:
On a positive note: the loops are NOT polyester, but cotton, so the potholders came out nice 'n thick and heavy.
I can see why posters said they lasted a long time. They probably will.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I gave this PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Building and Coding - Construction Kit with Puzzles, Augmented Reality to my 7 year old son as a gift from Santa. In comparison to other robot building kits, I wasn't that impressed. First of all, you MUST have an updated iOs or Android phone/tablet. I am unsure if Android has this problem, but if you have an iPhone 5 or 6 and you can't update to the latest iOs, you will not be able to use this robot. Also, since this is an augmented reality app, I doubt that the Kindle Fire will work on this. The camera just isn't powerful enough. I ran into this problem with my son's Fire HD 10 for other AR programs. Next, when you unbox, there are no instructions. You have to go a website to get the instruction manual, which could have been printed on the two cards in the box that say go to the website for a manual. Finally, this does not come with a power source. There is a lithium battery and a USB cable, but you will have to have your own plug. Obviously, many of us will already have various plugs, but to have a designated plug would be nice considering the amount asked for this product.

Overall, my son's interest in this was limited. He's much more interested using his other building toys and finding ways for them to move. I think he feels limited in his creativity. You cannot use this without the App, so any ideas he has of incorporating other mediums to this has him frustrated. It's a nice idea. However, considering that I try to limit his screen time as well it would be nice to have an off screen option to play with this.
text_fidelity_b: PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based)

But still it is nice to have handy. I decided to get this set so we can bring it with us and then fold it up to put it away. Let's take a look.

BOARD
The board is nice. It is a good folding board. There are decent sized wells in it, and the end collection spots are good sized too. The finish is rough. It really is not nearly as smooth as it could be. However, it has a thin coating on it that helps a bit.

CLASP
The clasp on mine works well.

GLASS PIECES
This has a carrying case with plenty of glass pieces in it. We play the 6 pieces per well version so having these pieces is helpful. There are many colors and finishes so you can have fun using it. There are more pieces than we use so if any break, there are plenty to replace them with.

INSTRUCTIONS
The instructions are basic, but doable. I suggest looking online for more details if you prefer to learn different ways to play.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you like mancala, this is a fun game. The board is a bit rough in finish, but this is still decent for a quick game. There are plenty of pieces.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I wish there was a way to store the pieces with the board instead of a separate bag. I will have to get a case of some sort to store this in for easy carrying and to keep these together. I also wish the sanding was a bit better on this and finish too.

It was a little hard to tell exactly what the process was of making them just by looking at the pictures, and It was actually a bit more difficult than I assumed.

So you take the colored film paper, trace the shape out of the book, cut it out, then place it on the sticky paper to puzzle all the colored pieces together like a mosaic, to make up the whole picture. You youths choose to do them any color you want, but the more colors you use to make up the picture, the more patience and precision you will need.
We started off simple with the strawberry (only 2 colors) which was pretty easy.
I went to apply the puff paint and it would not come out of the top of the tube. I tried to cut the nozzle down, squeeze it out slow which ended in it coming out the side of the bottle, and getting all over my fingers. It was so thick, I assumed it got semi dried out, so I threw it away to prevent any further mess.
Since we were unable to use the puff paint, my daughter outlined the strawberry with black sharpie. Unfortunately without the puff paint, the film paper is pretty flimsy.
Even though we did not get the full effect of the project, we still had some fun doing the craft together.

Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets This word game is for 3 – 5 players. It’s for ages 10 and up. Takes 30-minutes to play.

It comes in a cardboard box measuring just under 10” X 6.25” X 2.25”. It’s part of the United States Playing Card company, which makes Bicycle playing cards. Made in China.

Each player receives chips, totaling 30-points, to start. You also receive two cards. From there you go around and each person “pays” for additional cards. Cards with letters which are worth more. . . cost more. You go around four-times. At the end, everyone turns-over their cards and you have thirty-seconds to spell a word with the most points. Please Note: Timer not included. Whomever wins that round gets chips equaling the number of points for their winning word. Then the second place person receives chips worth their number and so on. After playing three times, the person with the most points wins.

FYI. . . This came was originally going to be called “The World Series of AlphaBets”. . . but somewhere along the way they changed it to “Fumbling Ferrets”, probably to make it sound more “family friendly”. But it has nothing to do with ferrets.

If you like word / spelling games, then this one is fairly easy and fast to play. If you’re playing with younger kids, especially to start, you may wish to extend the timer to come-up with a word by a little bit and then shorten it with each round.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets

Hot Wheels Track Set with 1:64 Scale Toy Firetruck, City Fire Station with Dragon Nemesis and Track Play, Dragon Drive Firefight We've owned plenty of hotwheels sets, some pretty standard and some pretty creative. This is one of those interesting ones I couldn't really understand until we got it. The car is sort of on an "assisted loop", in that there are points that require your intervention to continue. It starts off being "spit out" by the dragon, then fired from a booth, then launched up a loop, and- if everything goes according to plan - it lands on the head of the dragon which will either fall forward or to the side (not knowing which way is part of the fun). However, if you don't have everything 100% seated properly, it just fails miserably. My kids had trouble getting it to work until I came and reseated some parts more forcefully, but even then we still had a few misfires that caused it not to work.
But I suppose that's the tradeoff of the more obscure track sets, sometimes they are more difficult to operate successfully. Part of the fun is making it work, I think. But if you have a kid who isn't up for that challenge, maybe this isn't the set for them. We actually really liked it, and the payoff when it DOES work is the sort of moment that gets high fives and cheers all around.

Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5 This is a precious little game that I imagine young children will long remember.

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Paw Patrol Marshall's Transforming Fire Truck with Pop-Out Water Cannons, for Ages 3 and Up I felt like I needed a Paw Patrol car lesson while shopping for cars to fit in the Lookout Tower. Let me tell you there are three main lines I found on Amazon, Spin Masters website, and in Target/Walmart:
- Basic Vehicles
- Transforming Vehicles
- Ultimate Rescue Vehicles

I wanted cars that would fit the Lookout Tower, and finally figured out that although some people may say that the Ultimate Rescue line fits in the tower, they are the biggest of the three lines and some reviews say those are too big.
The Basic Vehicles are the original vehicles (the Basic Chase car comes with the Lookout Tower) and those were originally intended to be the cars for the tower. The Basic Marshall car is simply called “Marshall’s Fire Fightin Truck”. However, the Basic line is hardest to find, and they are currently either marked up by third party sellers on Amazon or I could only find one or two Basic cars at each Target I visited.

Enter this Transforming line. They are a bit smaller than the Ultimate Rescue, and I was able to find them for $12.99 each on Amazon. They all have a little button that pops out the pups gear. My kids like popping out Marshall’s water cannons and they can reset them themselves (ages 2.5 and 4).

Long story short, this will work in the Lookout Tower. Best of luck finding them all for your kid.

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game I am a board game afficionado. I own over 200 different strategy, social or silly games, and you'd better believe that my daughter is a gamer in waiting. Of course, as a young boy, Pretty Pretty Princess wasn't on my radar for myself, but I knew the name and the concept, and when it was my time to find a copy for my kid, there's no way I was paying the multiple hundreds for the original 80's item.

So I was thrilled when an appropriately priced remake made it's way to my house, and all it took was reading the name to hook my daughter (and interestingly, my wife as well) into a quest to become the most beautiful in all the realm.

The box for this one opens upside down for some reason, and one you get inside, you'll find a spinner, an odd, nearly blank game board, and some teeny tiny jewels to bling out your ensemble. Play is simple - you spin the spinner, attempt to move aroudn the circular board to earn all your gems, and the first one to get everything is crowned (literally) the prettiest princess.

Perhaps the most striking thing is the lack of effort they put into the board and spinner. Both are of reasonable thickness and sturdy, but there is almost nothing on the board in terms of graphic design outside of the logo on the field of white, and the spinner is literally numbers. They may have changed the font away from Times New Roman, but that's all there is to it. It looks like a high school kid's graphic design project, and not one that's going to earn high marks from the teacher.

That said, it's good to have this game back in print again, even if the game play is not particularly solid, and even if the graphics leave quite a bit to be desired. As I said, all I needed to do to get my little one to play was to tell her the name of the game, and my wife jumped right in on the nostalgia boat as well.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game

Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone This is an easy-to-learn game with minimal set-up. It’s fast-paced and the rounds and the games go quickly. The circular game board has letters from which to select and a 10-second time. A player draws a card and picks one of two categories to play, such as “Pizza Toppings”. The first player thinks of something that fits that category, such as “Cheese”, and presses the “C” on the board. The next player now needs to think of a pizza topping, but can’t use the letter “C”. Play continues until only one player remains. Then, the round is over and the next player chooses a card.

The game requires 2 “AA” batteries that are not included. There is a storage place on the bottom of the game board for the cards. If the timer wasn’t so loud, it would be a great game for the car. It would be good to bring on a trip to play once you arrived, since it’s compact with self-contained storage for the cards. This is a great game for families because the cards are double-sides with different difficulty levels on each side.

It was harder than it seems to come up with things that fit the category beginning with one of the available letters, within the time-limit. Younger kids may get bored after a few rounds, but great game for passing a short amount of time. It would be nice if it came with more cards, because if it did become a family favorite, it wouldn’t take long to go through the cards. Still, it’s a fun family game.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

text_fidelity_a: Melissa & Doug Farm Sound Puzzle - Wooden Peg Puzzle With Sound Effects (8 pcs) [[VIDEOID:cd72f835dae1d0a3c3f6f6b497d37389]] This is the least child intuitive toy I have ever encountered. Shame on Melissa and Doug- a company that big should have tested this one out before producing. Here's how this puzzle works- as you REMOVE the pieces, the song plays "old mcdonald" but apparently you need to teach your toddler to remove it in the CORRECT order, starting with the farmer and WAITING after removing each piece to hear the song play. Now if you child removes it too quickly they obviously miss all the sounds- if they even hear them within the song. I was expecting to TEACH my toddler animal sounds by hearing them as he placed the pieces. NO such luck. Who in their right mind made a puzzle that plays the sounds when you TAKE out pieces? Most of the kids dump it over so they can make the puzzle. And then there are no sounds when the pieces are placed, disappointingly. Wish I had read reviews, but who would think that Melissa and Doug could RUIN a classic sound puzzle? Somehow, they managed it.

text_fidelity_a:
SmartLab Toys That's Gross Science Lab this is still a good starter book on a difficult but important topic.
Science is a great subject that all need to learn better and That’s Gross Science Lab attempts to bring the fun of learning to curious kids. It encourages kids to conduct science experiments, each with an emphasis on learning and on creating something, well, gross and disgusting.

My girls love the subject of science and they did like this science set when it was introduced to them for the first time. I was a little disappointed when I opened the box and found it contained so little. You get three molds- one for barf, one for a centipede, and one for a maggot; a toilet mixer; a plastic jar; a bubble wand; spoon; two beakers and a stand. A small booklet with experiment ideas gets kids and parents started so they can create and laugh at so many gross things.

With the experiments, there are a total of 20 and some of them are fun for kids. But one problem I have is that every single one of them requires household ingredients, which you may or may not have. We were still able to do some of them right away because all they required was baking soda, corn starch, eggs, etc. But others required a special visit to the store and this could be upsetting to children and parents who want to open the box and start experimenting immediately.

What you get with this science kit isn’t much, but I must admit that it does get kids interested in science even more than before. In fact, that might be the most compelling reason to buy this science kit. It helps pique kids’ interests and makes them want to investigate more about the world around them. Other than that, this is a toy of average worth that may or may not satisfy those who buy it.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys That's Gross Science Lab

text_fidelity_a: Pass the Stache Board Game Watching a group of 13 year olds play Moustache Smash is like watching a Black Friday sale with everyone fighting for the same discounted towels. I couldn't help but laugh hysterically as each girl held the mustache up to her face then frantically tried to be the first to smash the card that either matched the color or the shape of their mustache. (Mind you they had to remember which mustache they chose and what it looked like because they have to keep it up on their face at all times when the game is in play - until it's time to snatch a card). The game comes with 6 mustaches on very solid plastic sticks. There is a suction cup at the end of the mustache that allows the playing card to be snatched up quite easily. It's best to play on a solid surface to make sure the card stays put. There are 32 mustache cards of various colors and shapes. Each player takes a turn being the dealer. The dealer flips the card over for all to see - but can't cheat by flipping the card facing them first. IF a player accidentally snatches up the wrong mustache, they have to return it plus two more mustaches (if they have them) from their stash. It goes into a pot for the next player who correctly snatches up a mustache to claim. When all 32 cards are dealt, the game is over. The player left standing with the most 'stashes wins. The cards are in perfect squares - keeping the field even for all players. The mustaches feel rubbery so are less likely to cause harm if accidentally smacked into another players hand. The one thing I suggest is you have the camera at the ready! I have some great video and excellent pictures that I was able to share with the players' parents. Unfortunately, without the parents' permissions, I cannot display any of the videos or photos. They weren't comfortable with their children being seen. The recommended age is 7 and up, but I can easily see a 5 year old handling this well. I would also be willing to play with a group of adults. For $15.99 with free prime shipping, it is a great birthday or Christmas gift without breaking the budget. Plus, there are no tiny pieces to lose or step on. (BONUS!)  Keep in mind, though, that there are only 6 mustaches... so a max of 6 players can play at one time.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women I could not tell exactly how these “puzzles” work, even after looking at the video. You have to do two different things. First you have to “flip” each of the circles back-and-forth until you get all of them flipped to the correct side. Then you have to “spin” each of the circles to align them correctly. I find that it’s best to start from the outside circle and work your way in. The “puzzles” with most similar colors / designs on each side are the most challenging to work to get the circles on the correct side.

FYI. . . Once you have completed one side, the opposite side will not be complete. So though you will not have to flip the circles. . You’ll have to rotate the circles to complete the puzzle. So you’ll always have one side complete, and one size incomplete.

It should be noted that this “puzzle” is sturdy enough for a puzzle such as this, but it can certainly be pulled apart and broken without too much effort.

I think this “puzzle” to be best for ages tweens and up. It’s not super challenging, but again the ones with the common colors on both sides are the most challenging.

This puzzle is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women

text_fidelity_a: Hauck Fire Rescue Pedal Go Kart Overall, I would say that I like the finished product of this kart, but the process wasn't the most pleasant. The directions are terrible--that was the worst part of the item. The directions are small pictures, with smaller pictures of items and the labeled part letter and numbers, making it hard to see. For example, there are nuts that have to be screwed onto the wheels and the picture is so small that you cannot see which end of the nut should go on the outside/ inside. I had to look very hard and make the best guess. Also, there are no words. I truly prefer words and pictures with directions so that I am clear especially for something that my child will be riding on. However, despite all of that the item is sturdy, looks good, and rides well. I put the seat on the last holes for my 5 year old (almost 6) who is 4' tall and it works well for him. However, I dont think any kid too much taller would be able to ride it comfortably. His legs are a little bent, and I dont see a kid up to 8 being able to ride this comfortably. It does ride over all kinds of surfaces, if they are flat or downhill. My son rode on flat grass (not the easiest but it did go), over rocks and concrete and it worked. Also the brake works very well, stops everytime even while going downhill.
text_fidelity_b: Hauck Fire Rescue Pedal Go Kart

text_fidelity_a:
White Mountain Puzzles The Eighties - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:b94eac5104dc142a073b662ff11284e3]] I loved this amazing puzzle. The artwork is fantastic! This is a painting of a whole bunch of pictures and other scenes and people from the 1980's. It's based on a painting by Jim Mellet, and his art is amazing! It takes a ton of scenes and people from the 1980's, and turns it into a wonderful painted collage.

The quality of the puzzle is top-notch. The pieces are very thick, and so they fit together well. In my video, you can see that I can actually pick up the entire puzzle, which is usually impossible to do with most puzzles. The backing is a nice blue color, so you can easily tell which pieces are upside down. The border is awesome. The puzzle is surrounded by a red and orange line. This makes the border really easy to put together, and it makes it very easy to identify the edge pieces.

The puzzle is challenging, but it's also very doable. In most puzzles, there's a huge spot of the same color that's very boring, and this puzzle didn't have any of this. I felt entertained and challenged throughout. It's also a great conversation starter, because it has so many iconic people and scenes. I especially liked the Atari, Donkey Kong, Pac-Man, and Mr. T.

Pros:
+Challenging, yet doable
+Fun events and people from the 1980's
+Excellent artwork
+High quality puzzle

text_fidelity_a:
Mainstreet Classics 18-Inch Backgammon Board Game Set The nicest part of this Main Street Classic Backgammon Set is the white topstitching on the black leatherette case which gives it a high quality look. Unfortunately, the set I received has a couple of creases in the fabric interior lining which continually attract my eyes and I always want to play the side without the creases. Because I'm a good sport, I always ask that my opponent select sides and I therefore always wind up with the creases to call my own. The set is not heavy and I appreciate the absence of a weighty and cumbersome handle, but if a handle is important to you for carrying, then this is not the set for you. The "stones" or round pieces have a nice weight to them and I also like the look and feel of all five dice. The cups are just fine in appearance and heft as long as you don't look at the workmanship closely, especially on the bottom where I fear the glue will not be effective for too long. The "manual" is extremely difficult to read because the imprint is faint and some of the words/diagrams are not legible, but as a plus, it does include a paragraph on the history of the game. With a better manual, I think I would have been more impressed with this set, but the included sheet of paper gives a very cheap and careless impression of the manufacturer. One can find resources for the game rules online or in game books and these are easier to read, so I'd suggest that if Main Street is not interested in providing worthwhile instructions, they'd be better off leaving this weak attempt out of the set.

All in all, the workmanship in stitching is excellent but the glue is lacking in the construction of the game I received. I enjoy playing the game, like the look of it, appreciate that it's far superior to the heavy pleather set I had many years ago, but I'm not excited about the retail cost.
text_fidelity_b: Mainstreet Classics 18-Inch Backgammon Board Game Set

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit I’m a big fan of the Thames & Kosmos building kits--especially the ones that teach STEM principles. However, this THAMES & KOSMOS PEPPER MINT IN THE FANTASTIC UNDERWATER SCIENCE VOYAGE EXPERIMENT KIT is definitely NOT one of my favorites. The experiments do teach about the physical properties of water (e.g., siphoning, hydraulics), but they are boring--mostly they require operating a syringe to push water through tubing.

The boat is easy to build. The parts are stamped onto thin sheets of wood. You punch the parts out of the sheets, and the edges come out smooth and clean. The parts then lock together without requiring glue or other fasteners. The assembly instructions are included in a booklet that contains a silly adventure/discovery story that features the girl character Pepper Mint.

The story is interrupted from time to time with instructions for science experiments. Each experiment has a good, easy-to-understand explanation of “what’s happening” (e.g., water can move things because, unlike air, it cannot be compressed).

The kit is apparently aimed at 11-year-old girls (Pepper Mint’s age), but the story and the experiments seem rather simplistic for that age group. I do wish that Thames & Kosmos had chosen a more serious name than “Pepper Mint” for their girl scientist. This kit has some teaching value, but it trivializes science for girls.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit
